name: PostHelp Images
author: Ernie St. Gelais

sections.description:
PostHelp Images removes the manual loop most people run today: go to ChatGPT, generate an image, download it, resize it in another tool, upload it to the media library, and type alt text by hand. PostHelp Images does all of that in one place.

It is human-in-the-loop by design. The AI suggests and generates; you review, refine, and place. It is a tool you drive from your own WordPress admin, not a fire-and-forget automation that floods your site with images.

What it does

  • Turns a loose idea into a vivid image prompt with one click, then lets you refine it in plain language before you spend a generation.
  • Starts from your own content: pick a post or page and it writes a short summary of it as the idea. A link under a post’s Featured Image box makes a new image for that post and sets it as the featured image.
  • Accepts an optional reference image, so the result can match a real truck, storefront or product.
  • Ships with five starter style templates (documentary photo, lifestyle photo, bright and airy photo, clean product shot, flat vector illustration). Save your own templates for the whole site, and new images start from your last used settings.
  • Generates through OpenAI in the same request you click Generate Image in, so no server cron is needed and it works on ordinary shared hosting.
  • Resizes to a maximum width and converts to WebP, JPEG, or PNG on your own server (Imagick preferred, GD fallback).
  • Writes short, concept-based alt text when you leave the field blank.
  • Adds the finished file to your media library with one click, or replaces an existing media library image in place, keeping its URL.
  • Imports a spreadsheet of image ideas as draft rows, with a dry-run preview, then generates the ones you select in one batch.

Bring your own OpenAI API key. The plugin works with your own OpenAI key and you pay OpenAI directly, usually a few cents per image. The Settings page explains how to get a key. The most secure setup is to define POSTHELP_IMAGES_OPENAI_KEY in wp-config.php. If you paste a key into Settings instead, it is encrypted at rest using your site salts and never shown again.

Or connect a free PostHelp account. If you would rather not set up an OpenAI account, click Connect PostHelp account in Settings. A new account gets 5 free images after you confirm your email. After that, images are sold in packs of 25 for $10 on posthelp.ai, with no subscription and no expiry. Your own OpenAI key always stays free to use, and when one is set it is always used first.

External services

This plugin connects to one of two services to create images and text, and sends nothing to either until you set it up.

OpenAI API (api.openai.com). Used when you have added your own OpenAI API key.

PostHelp (posthelp.ai), run by Sitez Incorporated. Used only after you click Connect PostHelp account in Settings and approve the connection, and only while no OpenAI key of your own is set. PostHelp then makes the OpenAI request for you with its own key and takes one image from your PostHelp balance per image created. Connecting sends your site’s admin address so the connection can be tied to your site, and the PostHelp account you create or log in to holds your email address. Disconnect at any time in Settings.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you click Generate Image: your prompt, the image style, and the output size and quality. If you picked a reference image, that image is sent too.
  • When you ask for a prompt suggestion, a content summary, alt text or a filename: your idea or prompt text. For a content summary, the text of the post or page you picked is sent.

The same information goes to PostHelp instead of OpenAI when you are using a connected PostHelp account. Settings also asks PostHelp for your remaining image count when you open it.

The plugin reads the chosen post or page from your own site to get its text. That request stays on your site.

OpenAI’s terms: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/
OpenAI’s privacy policy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/
PostHelp terms of service: https://posthelp.ai/terms-of-service/
PostHelp privacy policy: https://posthelp.ai/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin zip via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or install it from the plugin directory.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Add your OpenAI API key under PostHelp Images > Settings, or define POSTHELP_IMAGES_OPENAI_KEY in wp-config.php.
  4. Go to PostHelp Images > Add New, describe what you want, and click Generate Image.
sections.faq:
Do I need an OpenAI account?

No. You can add your own OpenAI API key, or connect a free PostHelp account in Settings and PostHelp makes the request for you.

What does it cost?

The plugin is free. With your own OpenAI key, you pay OpenAI directly, usually a few cents per image. With a PostHelp account, a new account gets 5 free images after you confirm your email. After that, images come in packs of 25 for $10 on posthelp.ai, with no subscription and no expiry.

I have my own key and a PostHelp account. Which one is used?

Your own key, always. PostHelp is only used when no key of your own is set.

Will it add images to my site on its own?

No. You review every image before it goes into your media library, and nothing is placed on a page for you. A spreadsheet import creates draft rows, and you pick which ones to generate.

Can it replace an image that is already on my site?

Yes. Replace in Media Library swaps the file and keeps the same URL, so every page that uses the image shows the new one. It only replaces files inside your uploads folder, and it backs up the original first.

Which image model does it use?

gpt-image-2.5-flare by default. You can change it in Settings.

Does it need server cron?

No. Each image is generated in the same request you click Generate Image in.

Where are my generated files stored?

In wp-content/uploads/posthelp-images/. Once you click Add to Media Library, the file becomes a normal WordPress attachment.

What sizes can I request?

Any width and height within the model’s limits, or an aspect preset. The plugin snaps a request to the nearest legal size and tells you what it used.

Is my API key safe?

The wp-config constant never touches the database. A key pasted into Settings is encrypted at rest. No plugin can fully protect a stored secret from someone who already controls your database and files, so the wp-config option is the real recommendation.
sections.changelog:
1.5.1

  • Image costs now show only on sites that use their own OpenAI key. With no key of your own, the Cost column in the images list and the cost in the result box are hidden.
  • Security hardening: every admin request checks your permission and a security token directly, including the sample CSV download and the Featured Image link.
  • Replace in Media Library only writes to the selected image’s own file inside your uploads folder, using the WordPress filesystem API.
  • The edit screen’s small style fix now loads through the WordPress stylesheet system.
  • With your own OpenAI key set, Settings no longer shows the PostHelp Account section, and images that failed only because free PostHelp images ran out are cleared so they can be generated with your key.

1.5.0

  • Connect a free PostHelp account from Settings instead of using your own OpenAI key. New accounts get 5 free images after confirming their email, and more are available in packs of 25.
  • When no OpenAI key is set and an account is connected, images, prompt suggestions, alt text and filenames are made through PostHelp. Your own key is always used first when one is set.
  • Running out of PostHelp images never locks anything. The message explains how to add your own key or buy more.

1.4.2

  • The default image model is now gpt-image-2.5-flare, which matched gpt-image-2 on quality in our tests at about a quarter of the cost per image. You can still type gpt-image-2 or any other model into Settings.

1.4.1

  • The text model for prompt suggestions, refine, filenames and alt text moves from gpt-5-mini, which OpenAI retires on December 11, 2026, to gpt-6-luna. A site with gpt-5-mini saved in Settings is moved over automatically.
  • Images made with gpt-image-2.5-flare or gpt-image-2.5-sunburst now record their cost.

1.4.0

  • Rows that were saved but never generated now show Draft. Queued appears only while a row waits in a running batch.
  • Five starter style templates.
  • How to get an OpenAI API key, on the Settings page.
  • Size presets no longer start wider than your Max width.
  • Removed the self-hosted update checker. Updates come from the plugin directory.
  • PostHelp Images now always uses its own OpenAI key and no longer falls back to the shared PostHelp key.

1.3.0

  • Start from content, featured image link, reference image, and replace in media library.

1.2.0

  • Concept-based alt text, a site default image style, shared templates, and Last used settings.

1.1.1

  • Removed unused code.

1.1.0

  • 16:10 preset and a build script.

1.0.0

  • First release.

short_description: Generate AI images, resize and convert them to web-ready files, and place them in your media library with alt text already set - all inside wp-admin.
